title: Present perfect continuous
titleVi: Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn
summary: Diễn tả hành động kéo dài đến hiện tại và giải thích kết quả trước mắt — cấu trúc ăn điểm trong Task 1 và Task 2.
whyItMatters: Khi bạn viết *House prices have been rising since 2015*, bạn vừa nêu xu hướng vừa ngầm nói rằng nó vẫn đang tiếp diễn — điều mà `present perfect simple` không làm rõ. Đây là thì giúp câu văn học thuật có chiều sâu thời gian, và là điểm khác biệt rõ nhất giữa band 6.5 và 7.5.

sections.heading: Form and core meaning: an activity running up to now
body: The present perfect continuous is **have/has been + -ing**. It presents an activity that started in the past and is still in progress, or has just stopped and still matters now.
The emphasis is on the *activity and its duration*, not on a completed result. *I've been writing the report* tells you what occupied my time; *I've written the report* tells you it is finished.
Because the action is unfinished, this tense almost always looks unfinished in time too: it pairs with *for*, *since*, *all day*, *recently*, *lately*.

examples.right: The city has been investing in public transport since 2016.
Researchers have been monitoring air quality for three years.
I've been reading the same report all morning.
She has been working here since she graduated.
examples.wrong: She is working here since she graduated.
examples.note: **since** + starting point requires a perfect form.

sections.heading: How long: for, since and the question form
body: **for** answers *how long*; **since** answers *from when*. Both are at home with the continuous when the situation is still true.
The natural question is *How long have you been ...?* — and the answer normally repeats the same tense: *I've been studying English for six years.*
A common Vietnamese-learner error is to answer a *how long* question with the present simple or the present continuous. Both sound wrong in English because the period reaches the present moment.

rows: They have been negotiating for three years.
The plant has been operating since 2018.
the whole period up to now
It has been raining all day.

sections.heading: Continuous versus simple: activity or result
body: Both tenses can describe the same situation, but they answer different questions. The continuous answers *what have you been doing?*; the simple answers *what have you done?*

Use the simple form when you care about **how much, how many, or whether it is finished**: *I've written three chapters.* Use the continuous when you care about **how long or how tiring it was**: *I've been writing all day.*
With *just* and *already*, the simple form is normal because the result is the point: *She has just finished the proposal.*

examples.right: I've been painting the flat, so the whole place smells of paint.
examples.note: Recent activity with a visible present effect.

examples.right: I've painted the flat — it's ready for the furniture.
They've been building the new bridge for two years.
examples.wrong: They've built the new bridge for two years.
examples.note: **for two years** with an unfinished project needs the continuous.

examples.right: She has just finished the proposal.
examples.wrong: She has just been finishing the proposal.

sections.heading: Explaining present evidence
body: A very natural use is to explain something visible right now: *Your eyes are red — have you been crying?* The activity is offered as the cause of the present state.
This pattern is useful in Task 2 when you describe a consequence: *Coastal cities have been expanding rapidly, which is why flood damage has become so expensive.*
Do not use it for single completed events. *I've been breaking my leg* is impossible; a broken leg is a result, so say *I've broken my leg*.

examples.right: The streets are wet — it has been raining.
examples.note: Visible evidence explained by a recent activity.

examples.right: You look exhausted. Have you been working all night?
examples.note: Question form of the same pattern.

examples.right: I've broken my leg, so I can't play on Saturday.
examples.wrong: I've been breaking my leg, so I can't play on Saturday.
examples.note: A single completed event with a result → simple form.

sections.heading: Stative verbs and the limits of the continuous
body: Stative verbs (*know, believe, own, belong, consist of, contain*) do not take the continuous, so they stay in the simple perfect: *I've known her for years*, never *I've been knowing her*.
A few verbs shift meaning. *I've been having trouble with the software* is acceptable because *have trouble* is an experience, not possession; but *I've been having a car* is not.
In formal writing, the continuous can sound informal if overused. One or two instances per paragraph create a sense of process; five make the essay feel like a diary.

examples.right: The committee has known about the risk for months.
examples.wrong: The committee has been knowing about the risk for months.

examples.right: The region has been experiencing unusually dry winters.
The building has belonged to the university since 1975.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have been knowing him for ten years.
commonMistakes.right: I have known him for ten years.
commonMistakes.why: `know` là stative verb, không dùng dạng tiếp diễn. Người Việt dịch 'tôi đã quen anh ấy được mười năm' và giữ nguyên cấu trúc tiếp diễn.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have been living here since ten years.
commonMistakes.right: I have been living here for ten years.
commonMistakes.why: `since` đi với mốc thời điểm, `for` đi với khoảng thời gian. Nhầm `since` và `for` là lỗi phổ biến nhất trong nhóm thì hoàn thành.

commonMistakes.wrong: She has been studied English for three years.
commonMistakes.right: She has been studying English for three years.
commonMistakes.why: Sau `have/has been` phải là V-ing, không phải V3. Cấu trúc đúng là `have/has been + V-ing`, không phải `have/has been + V3`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have been finishing my essay, so I can relax now.
commonMistakes.right: I have finished my essay, so I can relax now.
commonMistakes.why: Kết quả đã hoàn tất cần `present perfect simple`. Dùng tiếp diễn hàm ý bài luận vẫn còn đang viết dở.

commonMistakes.wrong: How long are you working for this company?
commonMistakes.right: How long have you been working for this company?
commonMistakes.why: Câu hỏi về khoảng thời gian kéo dài đến hiện tại phải dùng thì hoàn thành. Tiếng Việt dùng 'đang làm' nên người học dễ bê nguyên `present continuous` sang.

ieltsTips: Trong Task 1, dùng `has/have been + V-ing` khi xu hướng bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn tiếp diễn ở năm cuối của biểu đồ: *Emissions have been falling since 2015.*
Trong Task 2, dùng thì này để mô tả quá trình đang diễn ra và hệ quả của nó: *Cities have been growing faster than their infrastructure.*
Tránh dùng `present perfect continuous` cho số liệu đã chốt; nếu bạn nêu con số cụ thể của một giai đoạn đã kết thúc, hãy dùng `past simple`.
Khi phân vân, hỏi bản thân: người đọc cần biết *đã xong chưa* (simple) hay *kéo dài bao lâu* (continuous)? Chọn theo tiêu điểm, không theo thói quen.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses a state verb correctly with 'since'?
options: I have been knowing her since 2015.
exercises.explanation: **know** là stative verb nên dùng **present perfect simple**, không dùng tiếp diễn.

exercises.question: Which sentence emphasises how long an activity has lasted?
options: I have been writing all morning.
I will write a chapter tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: **have been writing all morning** nhấn mạnh thời lượng của hoạt động, không nhấn mạnh kết quả.

exercises.question: The pavement is wet. Which sentence explains it best?
exercises.explanation: Hoạt động vừa diễn ra và để lại dấu hiệu trước mắt → **present perfect continuous**.

exercises.question: Choose the sentence with the correct time preposition.
options: They have been negotiating since three years.
They have been negotiating for three years.
They are negotiating since three years.
exercises.explanation: **for** + khoảng thời gian; **since** + mốc thời điểm.

exercises.question: Which sentence reports a finished result?
options: She has been finishing the report.
exercises.explanation: Kết quả đã hoàn tất dùng **present perfect simple**.

exercises.question: House prices ___ (rise) steadily since 2016.
exercises.hint: since 2016 + xu hướng còn tiếp diễn
exercises.explanation: Xu hướng bắt đầu năm 2016 và vẫn tiếp tục → present perfect continuous số nhiều.

exercises.question: I ___ (work) on this essay for four hours and I still have two paragraphs to go.
exercises.hint: for four hours + vẫn chưa xong
exercises.explanation: Hoạt động kéo dài và chưa hoàn tất → present perfect continuous.

exercises.question: The research team ___ (collect) data since January, and the sample now covers 2,000 households.
exercises.explanation: Chủ ngữ số ít **team** + hoạt động kéo dài → **has been collecting**.

exercises.question: Sorry for the delay — we ___ (discuss) your proposal all morning.
exercises.explanation: **all morning** nhấn mạnh thời lượng của hoạt động vừa diễn ra.

exercises.question: The government ___ (know) about the shortage for months but has not acted.
exercises.explanation: **know** không có dạng tiếp diễn → present perfect simple.
